title: One batch of this recipe will make around 12- 15 cookies depending on...
description: One batch of this recipe will make around 12- 15 cookies depending on how thick you roll them. Recipe .... 200g real block butter (I prefer salted but it's preference) 200g castor sugar (granulated will also work) 420g plain (all purpose) flour  1 large egg To add flavour use a splash of vanilla, lemon ect extract.
transcript: quick and easy sugar cookie recipe great for wedding favors baby shower cookies or just to eat so you want 200 grams of sugar 200 grams of butter 410 grams of plain flour and one large egg so whisk your butter and sugar on high for around five minutes until nice light and fluffy then add in the egg and then the flour once all combined mix this together on high for around five minutes to form a dough the dough will look quite crumbly but with a good need it'll all come together beautifully so get this out on your work surface and give it a little need I've made a huge batch here so I will break off a little bit so it's more manageable to roll out I put between two sheets of parchment paper this just stops it from sticking to the work surface and everything else you can sprinkle the work surface with a bit of flour also to stop it from sticking now if you don't have cookie spacers like I don't I use two cake dowels just to place it either side of the dough to make sure that everything's rolled out evenly once nice and smooth I trim off any uneven bits this can be rolled up and used again and I pop in the fridge for around 10 minutes just to firm the butter up because I find that when cutting shapes out if the dough is a little bit firmer the shapes come out neater so when cutting your shapes out if you just run your fingers around the cutter as well it just gets rid of any jagged the edges I've preheated my oven to around 160 degrees fan and they take around 10 to 12 minutes to bake you're looking for just a slight golden edge just scrunch up and we need any leftover cookie dough and you can make more cookies with it so you want to let these completely cool before you start decorating and take them off the baking tray as soon as possible to let them cool a little tip as well sometimes if they've spread a little bit just use a cookie cutter and just go around the cookie a little bit while they're still warm and it should just bring them back to shape again now I use any fondant to decorate sugar cookies just make sure you give it a good knead so that it's nice and pliable I then cover my work surface in corn flour to roll out on when rolling out fondant just make sure you roll it and twist it and roll it and twist it to stop it from sticking to anything so this is a little acupuncture needle and it just enables you to pop any air bubbles without leaving a hole so smooth everything out when you're ready now I make sure my cookies fit this personalised topper I had made and it's just for a wedding so it says the couple's new name and I'm gonna stamp these out onto the fondant now make sure you leave enough space in between each one to cut them out and when you're ready to start stamping the shapes out just make sure your fondant isn't stuck to the work surface when cutting out as well if you're using a circle just twist the cutter slightly from side to side and again this just makes sure that everything comes out super neat and then I'll also once it's ready to come up I will run my finger around the edge just to get rid of any jaggedy edges so these are now ready to go on top of my cooled cookies I add a little water to get them to stick but you can use jam you can use buttercream anything merely edible obviously but water works perfectly and then once these have firmed up slightly I will be bagging them individually look at them all together I had about 200 of these to make so I was just showing them off showing off with them all together so and to bag them up I've ordered some food safe clear plastic bags and use some little ties to keep them airtight and the theme of this wedding had a champagne gold colour so I ordered in some little champagne gold bows and just use a hot blue gun to add a tiny dot of blue and attach the bow so these are they taste very similar to a shortbread but a lot easier to make and these will stay fresh for at least a week look at them beautiful and they taste delicious too
